Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

iCARE 2.0.0 (unofficial distribution)

The first release of this unofficial, refactored distribution of iCARE. It is rewritten from scratch on the basis of Bioconductor iCARE 1.40.0 and of 1.33.1.9002, a patched development version prepared by the maintainer of this distribution. The functions, their arguments and the names of their results are unchanged. vignette("differences") explains each change below.

Changes that can alter results

  • The reference weights (model.ref.dataset.weights) are used correctly in the calibration of the baseline hazard; the official version scrambled non-uniform weights across subjects and ages.
  • Fractional start ages and interval lengths are used exactly, instead of rounding a fractional start up and counting a fraction of a year as a whole year.
  • Rates are needed only for the years of age inside the intervals. In the official version, a missing rate at the age where an interval ends made the risks NA or, when intervals differed, silently replaced the risk of every profile by the average over its percentile bin; this also affected the risks that ModelValidation() computed for the example studies.
  • For a profile with missing risk factors, the risk combines the profile’s own observed risk factors with the donors’ values of the missing ones, as in the published method (Pal Choudhury et al. 2020, equation 3), instead of averaging the donors’ own risks. Risks of profiles in the tails of the risk distribution can change by more than 10%.
  • Each profile with missing risk factors gets the risk over its own interval, independently of the other profiles.
  • Rates given by age band are read as yearly rates for every age of the band.
  • For SNP-only models, refs.risk holds the risks of simulated people instead of averages over the n.imp sets of simulated people.
  • computeAbsoluteRiskSplitInterval() combines the two intervals as AR1 + S1 * AR2, accounting for death from other causes before the cut age, and keeps the reference weights after the cut age.
  • ModelValidation():
    • the AUC counts tied risk scores as 1/2;
    • the Hosmer-Lemeshow statistic uses the variance under the null hypothesis by default (hosmer.lemeshow.variance = "observed" restores the earlier statistic);
    • in sampled studies, the E/O confidence interval accounts for the variability of E;
    • risk-score groups handle tied scores and empty groups, and the degrees of freedom of the tests follow the number of groups formed;
    • the study incidence is the person-time rate by attained age, with confidence intervals;
    • a supplied predicted.risk or linear.predictor is never recomputed, the reference weights and n.imp of the model object are used, and onsets after exit are censored consistently;
    • cases diagnosed at exit are kept when ages have decimals (rounding error in exit minus entry turned many of them into non-cases);
    • the reference population’s risks use each row’s own window.

New features

  • Category_Results has numeric columns and adds each group’s E/O ratio with its confidence interval and the numbers of subjects and cases; Category_Specific_Expected_to_Observed_Ratio is new.
  • plotModelValidation() is redrawn with ggplot2 and patchwork: square panels with their statistics, incidence by attained age, an optional panel of E/O by risk group (panels), base.size, and the figure is returned for saving with ggplot2::ggsave().
  • print(), summary() and plot() methods for the results of computeAbsoluteRisk(), computeAbsoluteRiskSplitInterval() and ModelValidation().
  • The calibrated baseline hazard is returned as attr(result, "calibration").
  • With SNPs, family history may be coded in any way, for example as a factor with reference level “1” (the official version stopped with an error); the attenuation of its log relative risk applies to the effect of family history.
  • Columns of apply.snp.profile named after the SNPs are matched by name.
  • Clear error messages for invalid inputs, including formulas that give infinite or undefined design values.

Implementation

  • Pure, vectorized R: the C code and the use.c.code option are removed (the option is accepted with a deprecation warning and ignored). Every benchmarked workload is faster than the official version with its compiled code; see vignette("performance").
  • plotrix, gtools and Hmisc are no longer dependencies; ggplot2 and patchwork are.
  • The code is organized in small documented modules (ages and rates, the covariate and SNP models, the risk engine, missing risk factors, and the validation statistics), with a test suite that compares the results with brute-force computations and with recorded outputs of earlier versions.
  • A simulation study (tools/simulations/validation-simulation.R) checks the coverage of the confidence intervals and the size of the tests of ModelValidation(). The relative-risk test, unchanged from earlier versions, rejects calibrated models too often when risk groups have few cases, and its documentation now says so.
